entries.name: Split-Stance Calf Rise — rapid rear-heel finish
entries.sourceName: Split-Stance Calf Rise — rapid rear-heel finish
entries.instruction: Produce rear-ankle force through the forefoot in a stable forward-oriented stance. Use stable hand support and a short split stance. Front foot stays flat; rear knee softly straight and rear forefoot planted. Rapidly lift the rear heel, hold 1 s and lower 2 s while the pelvis stays still. Three reps per rear leg; no stride or flight. Recovery: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 6 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section Use instead: an assisted single-leg straight-knee rapid heel rise at the same per-leg dose if the split stance does not load the rear ankle usefully. This replaces remaining work in this slot; follow an explicit replacement dose if stated, otherwise keep the remaining dose/rest. Log changed events or laterality.

exercises.description: Keep the working load at 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Load the turning arc and controlled endpoints that transmit lower-body force into the selected upper rotational action. Secure the landmine and qualify the bar, grip and minimum load. Hold the sleeve or suitable grip in both hands with elbows softly bent. Turn the feet and hips with a modest side-to-side loaded arc while keeping ribs over pelvis. Each one-way traverse is one rep; the return is the next counted rep. Take about 2 seconds per traverse and settle briefly at each endpoint. Avoid trunk lean, a trapped knee or an uncontrolled finish. Use instead: Reduce the load or arc for loss of alignment. If a secured, manageable landmine setup cannot be qualified, use a standing two-hand band rotation with a verified side anchor and the same one-way traverse counting instead; log the changed setup. Apply this change only to the same remaining combined dose and recovery; it replaces the original execution and adds no extra task or make-up attempts. This replacement uses only the remaining combined dose/rest unless explicitly stated; log changed support, event type, load and added time.

explosive_progression_note: Countermovement Jump — vertical rise and stick returns to the controlled countermovement vertical jump while Band Chest Press — mid-range pause into fast finish and Band Row — mid-range pause into fast finish shift the arm tasks to held mid-range starts and rapid finishes. The point-cued lower turn selects its direction before movement, leaving the main force work directed by organized support rather than a late reactive change. Compared with Class 27, prescribed ball releases change from 2 to 4, bilateral foot-landing events change from 0 to 6, explosive set/side bouts change from 10 to 11. After reviewing actual recovery, require the held arm start without strain, the two-foot reception to hold and the direction cue to arrive before the plant. Use the listed full-range light press or paused row only for remaining held-start attempts if their partial positions fail. Use a preannounced direction for remaining E5 attempts if cue errors disturb the plant, and retain the existing physical dose and rests.
